title: 2009 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 1
statement: How many ways can the integers from -7 to 7 be arranged in a sequence such that the absolute value of the numbers in the sequence is nondecreasing?

solutions.text: Each of the pairs \(a,-a\) must occur in increasing order of \(a\) for \(a=1, \ldots, 7\), but \(a\) can either occur before or after \(-a\), for a total of \(2^{7}=128\) possible sequences.
